summary: Python library that scrapes websites and documents with an LLM: describe what you want and get structured results.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ScrapeGraphAI is a Python scraping library that uses LLMs and graph pipelines to extract information from websites or local files. You give a prompt and a source, and it returns structured data.
sixtySeconds.problem: Traditional scrapers break whenever a page layout changes. ScrapeGraphAI lets you say what you want in plain language instead of writing selectors.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for several ready pipelines (such as SmartScraperGraph), support for local Ollama models or OpenAI, and an MIT license.
requirements: An LLM: local Ollama or an API key

overview: Install with pip, then run playwright install so it can fetch pages. Using a virtual environment avoids library conflicts.
SmartScraperGraph is the most common pipeline: give it a prompt, a source URL and a config naming the LLM (for example ollama/llama3.2, or openai/gpt-4o-mini with an API key), then call run().
Respect each website's terms and robots rules when scraping. The library is MIT licensed; a hosted service also exists.
limitations: LLM calls make it slower than plain scrapers

firstRun.title: Scrape a page with a local model
firstRun.code:
from scrapegraphai.graphs import SmartScraperGraph

graph_config = {
    "llm": {"model": "ollama/llama3.2", "model_tokens": 8192, "format": "json"},
    "verbose": True,
    "headless": False,
}

smart_scraper_graph = SmartScraperGraph(
    prompt="Extract useful information from the webpage, including a description of what the company does, founders and social media links",
    source="https://scrapegraphai.com/",
    config=graph_config,
)

print(smart_scraper_graph.run())
